sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text: Manufactures/trades condoms at Noida; took over Anondita Healthcare proprietorship under a 1 April 2024 business-transfer agreement. Reliable predecessor history can count, but it must be reconciled to listed-company and subsidiary perimeters rather than treating every growth percentage as organic. [S1]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
Prospectus standalone top-ten customers represented 99.46% of FY 25 revenue. Condom capacity is 562 m units annually on three shifts, while FY 25 production was 258.835 m, or 46.05%, on two shifts; reported output includes substandard scrap. FY 24/FY 23 utilization was 39.14%/32.80%. Thus reported capacity headroom is not saleable incremental output and does not itself prove profitable demand. Tender qualifications and quality controls provide entry friction, but concentrated government procurement creates pricing, payment and disqualification risk. The disclosed 2020 Rajasthan glove-supply debarment concerned the predecessor and was stayed by the High Court on January 22, 2021; it must not be represented as a current ban. [P1]

Cupid’s audited standalone FY 26 NSE filing shows revenue₹357.7088 cr, PAT₹108.2645 cr, other income₹33.6926 cr and finance cost₹2.8073 cr. Excluding all other income gives EBIT₹111.6115 cr,31.20% of sales; fair-value gains are part of non-operating earnings. Anondita consolidated operating EBIT is₹49.5852 cr,36.08% of sales, despite much smaller scale. Different trading/product/geographic mix and cash investments preclude blindly applying Cupid’s headline P/E. [PEER1][S1]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The final prospectus separates listed-company FY 25 standalone CFO ₹6.0796 cr from the predecessor proprietorship FY 24/FY 23 CFO ₹10.5488/−9.4963 cr. It separately identifies business-acquisition assets, liabilities and ₹7.3404 cr non-cash equity consideration within investing/financing presentation. The FY 25 consolidated annual-report CFO is not interchangeable with this standalone series. Consequently, simply summing the three years would manufacture a comparable cash-conversion ratio. The founder-business transfer and acquired subsidiary perimeter must be reconciled before numerical CASH/CAP scores. Acquisition consideration also must not be counted both as cash capex and newly issued shares. [P1][S1]

Annual report records FY 24/25/26 production 219.95/258.84/432.13 m pieces. FY 26 growth 66.95% supports real demand rather than merely selling-price inflation. Installed capacity rises 562→869 m, with 307 m addedFebruary 2026. Stated 80.67% utilization is not 432.13/869 (49.73%); its effective-capacity basis needs explanation. Do not call the full 869 m operational for the entire year. May call’s approximately 806 m conflicts with later annual 869 m, so annual is used with dated-source caveat. Female-product lines under trial are not yet demonstrated commercial revenue. [S1][CALL]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Actual rights gross₹91.02577 cr less LOF cost estimate₹5.4606 cr gives₹85.56517 cr before actual fee revision. LOF allocations are female capex₹50 cr,WC₹25.7496 cr,GCP₹9.7998 cr; the₹54.5801 cr project also needs₹4.5801 cr internal funds. Promoters declared renunciation rather than rights subscription. July warrants are separate, at₹1038, with only 25% upfront received. Models do not add unpaid proceeds without shares or treat financing as revenue. [LOF][S1]

Standard 25% operatingNOPAT₹37.1889 cr over average total equity-plus-debt₹115.2703 cr is 32.26%; incrementalNOPAT₹18.5181 cr over addedcapital₹99.2010 cr is 18.67%. These accounting proxies include IPO cash/CWIP timing, not mature project returns.₹62.8069 cr capex with low CFO and another₹54.5801 cr project require execution before strong reinvestment quality is proven. End-period total capital rose from₹65.6698 cr to₹164.8708 cr. Existing CWIP₹41.4950 cr is already an asset paid for, not a second future cash deduction. Future depreciation/capex and commissioning remain material forecast assumptions. [S1][LOF]

Brickwork assigns BBB/Stable and A 3 to₹56.21 cr facilities on a standalone approach. It calls liquidity adequate and reports about 60% average Deutsche facility utilization. Its FY 26 numbers are provisional, not consolidated audited substitutes. The rating explicitly identifies competitive branding costs, latex prices and regulatory/certification risk. It is contrary evidence to immediate-distress claims, not equity-price protection. [RATING]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
AGM materials include proposals expanding related-party transaction/guarantee limits, including a proposed limit rising from ₹60 cr to ₹75 cr. Approval ceilings are not actual cash transactions or proven diversion. Review executed guarantees, beneficiary entities, security, consideration and minority exposure against current net worth. [S1]

FY 26 consolidated related-party purchases include ₹9.1005802 cr from Anondita Healthcare partnership, ₹0.9520875 cr from Anondita Healthcare Products and ₹3.8298680 cr from Anondita Healthcare Pvt Ltd. Lease-rent rows total ₹3.614868 cr across the named partnership and products company. The partnership also has a ₹4.907403 cr short-term advance balance, and actual disclosed corporate guarantee for an associate car loan is ₹2.2 cr. These actual amounts differ from approval ceilings. Ownership-transfer notes retain certain property titles, deposits, vehicles and bank-guarantee arrangements in predecessor entities; this is a title/collection/enforcement diligence issue, not proof assets do not exist. Management describes litigation with Swear Healthcare as reciprocal disputes over glove-machine designs; allegations are not adjudicated findings. [S1]

CARE terminated IPO monitoring effective 7 December 2025 after citing untimely/incomplete information and breach of agreement. This is a real stewardship concern, not a routine rotation. Infomerics subsequently reports March IPO deployment:₹62.75 cr used,₹6.74 cr remaining; equipment 2.62/6.00, WC 35.75/37.78,GCP 16.14/17.38 cr. Replacement monitoring is a remedy, not proof the earlier information failure never happened. [TERM][MON]

September 24 letter withdrew the September 8 nullification and restored September 7 corrigendum: issue 958,166 shares, not 958,000. The 166-share difference is economically small, while correctoperativeallotment matters for reconciliation. Treat the latest superseding filing as authoritative; do not turn administrative revisions alone into allegations. [U2]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY 26 consolidated revenue₹137.4157 cr and PAT₹34.2965 cr compare with FY 25 ₹76.9907 cr/₹16.5047 cr. Reported CFO is₹10.6381 cr/−₹7.4041 cr. The two-column cash-flow layout places short-term borrowing changes−₹5.7522 cr/+₹15.3091 cr in financing, not operating activities. No borrowing reclassification is appropriate. FY 26 operating-profit-before-WC₹51.4032 cr minus net WC absorption₹37.3427 cr minus cash tax₹3.4224 cr reconciles CFO₹10.6381 cr. The verified layout supports using reported operating cash without reclassifying financing movements. [S1]

The May 29 revised filing changes the allocation between owners and minority interests, reserves and EPS, while management states aggregate profit and balance-sheet totals are unchanged. The annual report confirms FY 26 profit attributable to equity holders ₹33.4459681 cr, minority ₹0.8505738 cr, and weighted EPS ₹20.77. FY 25 owners profit is ₹15.8821162 cr. Valuation must use owners profit, not ₹34.2965 cr total group PAT. A correction affecting EPS matters to investors even if aggregate profit is unchanged; the corrected filed figures are used rather than treating the revision itself as an integrity failure. [R1][S1]

September 24 revised rights allotment adds 958,166 shares at ₹950, gross ₹91.02577 cr, taking paid-up shares from 18,086,618 to 19,044,784. July 8 allotment is 285,000 promoter warrants at ₹1,038, total exercise consideration ₹29.583 cr, 25% upfront (₹7.39575 cr) and 75% on exercise (₹22.18725 cr), within 18 months. Fully converted share count would be 19,329,784 before any further events. The exchange announcements reviewed through October 20 contain no subsequent conversion announcement, but this is not bank confirmation of proceeds. A model must include remaining exercise cash only when it also includes exercise dilution, and must trace rights deployment rather than treating gross proceeds as free surplus cash. [W1][U1][U2]

September 24 revisedrightsallotment is 958,166 shares at₹950, gross₹91.02577 cr. Issuedcapital increased from 18,086,618 to 19,044,784 shares, facevalue₹10. This post-March capital is the relevant startingpoint before any laterconversions, not weighted-averageEPSshares. Gross issuecash must be reconciled to issueexpenses, deployment and any connectedfinancing. [U1]

May 27 management attributes receivables to late-year government shipments and minimum 120-day collection, and expects exports with advances/LCs to improve cash. This explains growth funding but does not verify subsequent receipts. Management’s female-condom revenue/PAT aspirations are conditional on capacity, qualification and orders; they are not contracted sales or base forecasts. Follow actual collections and shipped volumes, not the ambition alone. [CALL]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Cupid is the prospectus operating peer, but the quoted 110.38 x P/E uses August 14, 2025 pricing and different scale/earnings; it is not an appropriate automatic exit multiple. With post-rights 19.044784 m shares, FY 26 owners profit implies EPS ₹17.56, below the historical weighted ₹20.77. At the October 19 ₹1,007.45 close, indicative equity value is ₹1,918.67 cr and trailing owner-earnings P/E about 57.4 x. On full warrant conversion, unchanged-profit EPS falls to ₹17.30, before earnings from the new cash. A five-year 15% price return without dividends requires ₹2,026.32; at an assumed 25 x exit multiple, that requires EPS ₹81.05, about 35.8% annual growth from post-rights EPS. This is a reverse hurdle, not a forecast or endorsed multiple. At unchanged owner profit and 20 x, value is about ₹351.2, roughly 65% below the dated close; halving profit at 15 x gives about ₹131.7, roughly 87% downside before further dilution. The completed linked model below uses verified financing and explicit deployment assumptions; the reverse hurdles are not forecasts. [P1][S1][U1][W1][M1]

Cupid’s audited standalone FY 26 NSE filing shows revenue₹357.7088 cr, PAT₹108.2645 cr, other income₹33.6926 cr and finance cost₹2.8073 cr. Excluding all other income gives EBIT₹111.6115 cr,31.20% of sales; fair-value gains are part of non-operating earnings. Anondita consolidated operating EBIT is₹49.5852 cr,36.08% of sales, despite much smaller scale. Different trading/product/geographic mix and cash investments preclude blindly applying Cupid’s headline P/E. [PEER1][S1]

At dated₹1007.45, conditional base/bear/bull terminal prices are₹952.75/₹138.77/₹2280.47, with annual returns-1.11%/-32.73%/17.75%. Base 15%-hurdle entry arithmetic₹473.68 is conditional, not a recommendation. Annual rows bridge tax, capex,WC,interest,debt and warrants; no final multiple is copied from Cupid. [S1][LOF][M1] Model correction, 20 October 2026: our earlier model omitted opening claims. The revised reference settles ₹0.0101103 crore at opening and deducts ₹0.1779931 crore of remaining net legacy employee obligations at terminal. These are corrections to our calculations, not changes to issuer-reported data. Future service expense remains funded through forecast margins. Accelerated settlement gives base return -1.1103% versus the reference -1.1103%. BQS, GQS, IAS and classification are unchanged. [S1]

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
Analyst stress: demand or export qualification disappoints while capacity/inventory, marketing and guarantees create cash obligations. Monitor actual unit sales, net realizations, product/channel concentration, returns and quality compliance, precursor-business adjustments, connected-company financing and genuinely operating cash. Completed canonical scores, linked price-based scenarios and reverse 5×/10× requirements are below; no multibagger designation follows.

Bear terminal₹138.77, severe₹20.96. Tender/collection failure and stranded new-product capex can create large permanent entry-price impairment despite rights cash.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five-times/ten-times₹1007.45 means₹5037.25/₹10074.50. At 25 x terminal P/E and current 1.9044784 cr shares, required ownerPAT is₹383.73/₹767.46 cr versus₹33.45 cr, approximately 62.9%/87.1% annual growth for five years. At 25% ownerPAT margin, sales₹1535/₹3070 cr are required. This exceeds the base funded path and requires exceptional qualification, demand, scale and cash collection; warrants increase the required total profit. No supported multibagger designation follows. [S1][LOF][M1]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Priorities: cash collected from large March receivables; exports shipped and LC/advance realization; female-project cost/qualification and commercial utilization; explicit denominator for 80.67% utilization; rights and warrant deployment; monitoring-agency information timeliness; connected-property/loan terms and completed title transfers. Thesis weakens if receivable growth outruns shipments, female output misses qualification milestones, or further capital is needed before existing projects earn cash. Growth quality is stronger than investment attractiveness at the dated premium valuation. [S1][CALL][MON][LOF]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Condom manufacturer with verified production and core-business growth, meaningful expansion funding and strong operating profit growth. Weak consolidated cash conversion, connected-party/property exposures and a past monitoring-information failure temper business quality; the high post-rights earnings multiple leaves little valuation protection even under substantial growth. Canonical BQS 5.32, Growth QualityGQS 6.6, conditional IAS 3.18. No persistent CASH cap imposed on only two comparable consolidated years. Earlier borrowing-adjusted CFO was a two-column layout error and is explicitly withdrawn.

Final published measures: BQS 5.32; GQS 6.6; IAS 3.18. Any change in price, funded cash deployment, share count or execution restrictions requires recomputation; these are conditional research classifications, not a trade instruction.

Female product qualification, utilization and market access remain forecasts; issuer patents/certifications do not assure economics. Core predecessor/standalone history is distinguished from consolidated subsidiary additions; consolidated cash history is shorter. No additional trajectory upgrade.

Two comparable years do not alone trigger persistent3–5year cap.

New female capacity remains unproved; cash collection, title transfers and monitoring history temper otherwise credible manufacturing progress. Annual utilization percentage needs an effective-capacity bridge.
